target.title: refactor(shared): consolidate lazy import memoizers
target.body:
Related: #98748

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a maintainability problem where lazy runtime imports repeatedly define module-level promise state and loader functions, while two shared helpers separately own the same cache behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds the direct `createLazyPromise` function API, makes the higher-level lazy runtime helpers delegate to that canonical cache owner, and preserves their existing sticky-rejection contract. The first bounded caller batch replaces all five manual memoizers in the public library entrypoint without changing dynamic import boundaries or plugin SDK exports.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Maintainers get one cache implementation for lazy runtime imports and a smaller, clearer library entrypoint; follow-up batches can migrate remaining duplicate memoizers package by package.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/lazy-promise.test.ts src/shared/lazy-runtime.test.ts` — 2 files, 8 tests passed.
- `pnpm build` — passed, including CLI bootstrap and plugin SDK export checks; no ineffective dynamic-import warning for this change.
- `pnpm check:import-cycles` — passed with 0 runtime value cycles.
- Fresh Codex autoreview — clean, no accepted/actionable findings, 0.96 confidence.
- Search proof — `src/library.ts` manual `??= import(...)` memoizers reduced from 5 to 0; repository production occurrences reduced from 280 to 275.
- Production LOC proof — touched production files changed by +20/-37 lines, a net reduction of 17 lines while establishing the canonical API.
